requirements.text: REQ-CALLS-SUCCEED: in a consistent state, every call succeeds: the policy hooks for any account, claims and speed changes never revert.
REQ-SUPPLY-HOOK: a supply hook brings the supply index up to date and credits `who` for exactly the supply rewards since its start (`accrualStart`), rounded down; nothing else changes.
REQ-BORROW-HOOK: a borrow hook brings the borrow index up to date and credits `who` for exactly the borrow rewards since its start, rounded down; nothing else changes.
REQ-CLAIM: a claim credits `who` on both sides as the hooks do and then pays it everything it has accrued when the Comptroller holds enough COMP.
REQ-SET-SPEEDS: a speed change accrues what was emitted at the old speed and then applies the new speeds.

REQ-REWARDS-BOUNDED: from the upgrade of any well-formed pre-upgrade state, after any sequence of operations, the COMP paid out to accounts plus the COMP accrued to them never exceeds what they held or had accrued before the upgrade, plus what they were owed at the upgrade, plus the COMP emitted since.

REQ-ACCOUNT-BOUNDED: the same for every single account: from the upgrade of any well-formed pre-upgrade state, no account ever holds or has accrued more COMP than it held or had accrued before the upgrade, plus what it was owed at the upgrade, plus the COMP emitted since.

REQ-NO-BACKDATED-REWARDS: an account is never credited for blocks before it held a position. In any state reached from the upgrade of a well-formed pre-upgrade state, if an account holds no position, then whatever happens next it gains at most the COMP emitted from then on.

trust_assumptions: Lean v4.35.0 kernel, compiler and runtime
the protected spec and locked challenge as reviewed by the owner
the executable wrapper (app/Main.lean) is TESTED_ONLY, not proved
scope: Properties are proved about the pure definitions comptroller in namespace CompRewards for all inputs; the executable comp-sidecar is built from the same source and tested, and its JSON wrapper is not proved.
